summary: Thesis log for the two satellites beyond the world sleeve: S&P 500 (CSPX.L, VUAA.L) and Nasdaq-100 (CNDX.L, EQAC). Verdict: S&P 500 intact, Nasdaq-100 intact. Cash-flow evidence is still strong: S&P 500 Q3 2026 blended earnings growth is 31.4% with a forward P/E of 17.7, the lowest since November 2023, and TSMC's October sales rose 59.7% year on year. The case has more pressure on it than last quarter: the 10-year yield touched 5.03% and a December Fed hike is priced, leaving an equity earnings yield (about 5.7%) barely above Treasuries. Nvidia, the largest weight in both indices, has an open board probe and an undecided CEO question ahead of its Nov 17 results. AI capex is moving onto debt (Goldman sees hyperscaler issuance rising from $250bn to $420bn in 2027). Democrats plan AI and data-center bills from January 2027, so far proposals only. No Nasdaq-100 or S&P 500 methodology change was found this week. Every item is weight 0 (record only), so all are severity 0.

events.issue: Governance risk at the largest index weight. Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on Nov 8 into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, and press reports on Nov 11 said the board would discuss his position. No decision has been announced. This is a single-name event, not a structural break in either index thesis; watch the Nov 17 results and any board outcome.

Cash-flow support for the thesis is intact. With 88% of companies reported, FactSet's blended Q3 2026 S&P 500 earnings growth is 31.4% and revenue growth 14.3%. CY2026 growth is estimated at 33.3%, and the forward P/E of 17.7 (Nov 5) is below its 5-year (19.8) and 10-year (19.1) averages.

The valuation margin over bonds has narrowed. The 10-year yield touched 5.03% after a hot October CPI on Nov 10, and CME FedWatch prices a December hike as near-certain. A forward earnings yield of about 5.7% (1/17.7) leaves an equity risk premium of under 1 point. This weighs most on long-duration mega-cap tech, so it hits the Nasdaq-100 sleeve harder.

AI capex is shifting to debt financing. PIMCO says AI borrowers are about half of long-dated US non-financial IG issuance, and Goldman sees hyperscaler bond issuance rising from about $250bn in 2026 toward $420bn in 2027. Separately, S&P put Meta on negative outlook (Oct 30). Higher leverage at the index's largest spenders raises the bar for future free cash flow.

Policy risk. Democrats, who take Congress in January 2027, plan bills on data-center electricity costs, independent testing of advanced AI models and AI-company liability (Reuters). These are proposals only: a presidential veto and Republican votes are obstacles. Recorded as a long-horizon risk to AI capex and mega-cap margins.

End-demand data for the AI build-out remains strong. TSMC's October 2026 revenue was NT$586.89bn, +59.7% YoY, and January-October was +43.3% YoY. This supports the cash-flow side of the Nasdaq-100 thesis despite the SOX drawdown (still about 28% below its June peak).
